sentences.text: With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 12.12.2022 passed in MACC No.16/21 by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua, whereby a total sum of Rs.18,61,360/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

3. As per the appellants, on 17.10.2022, at about 2:00 pm Virendra husband of appellant No.1 and father of appellants No.2 and 3, was going along with appellant No.3 on his motorcycle from his shop at Bhamrada colony to his house.

When they reached Kalyanpura, respondent No.1 drove motorcycle bearing registration No.MP- 45 MN 6895 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle, as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment but eventually expired.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9419 2 MA-1781-2023 4.
The appellants, thereafter, filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.13,49,6000/- to them by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondents by filing their written statements to the same.

Upon Smt. Kalavati vs Dhuliya on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40297744/
1 evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.

5. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the deduction of half which has been made by the claims tribunal towards personal expenses of the deceased, is illegal and erroneous.
The same ought to have been taken at 1/3rd since he was married at the time of the accident.
The dependency of half can be taken only when the deceased is unmarried.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra , learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal to the appellants, in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submission of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8. The deceased was admittedly married at the time of the accident and is survived by his widow and two sons.

The deduction towards personal expenses hence could have been done only to the extent of 1/3rd and not half as has been done by the claims tribunal in view of the decision of the Apex Court in the cases o f Sarla Verma and others vs Delhi Transport 2009 (6) SCC 121 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi 2017 (16) SCC 680.

sentences.text: Thus, the deduction NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9419 3 MA-1781-2023 towards personal expenses of the deceased deserves to be taken at 1/3rd only.
8. The appellants would be entitled for on account of loss of dependency Rs.4,88,960/- x 7 x 1/3rd which would be Rs.22,81,813/-.
The amount awarded to the appellants under the other heads by the claims tribunal is proper.
9. Thus, the appellants are entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.24,31,813/- to them by way of compensation whereas the claims tribunal has erred in awarding them a sum of Rs.18,61,360/- only.

The appellants are hence held entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.5,70,453/- which shall be paid to them along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
10. The appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.5 Lakhs whereas the enhancement in the amount of compensation has been made in the sum of Rs.5,70,453/-.
The appellants would hence be required to pay the requisite Court fees on the additional enhanced amount of Rs.70,453/- which shall be paid by them within a period of two months from today.
In case the Court fees is not paid as aforesaid, this enhanced amount of Rs.70,453/- shall cease to carry any interest after a period of two months.
11. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE jyoti Smt. Kalavati vs Dhuliya on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40297744/
